title: Chelsea’s Millie Bright retires with immediate effect as club’s longest-serving player
author: Jessica Hopkins
content:
Chelsea captain Millie Bright has retired with immediate effect after over a decade at the club.

The 32-year-old has ended her career as the Women’s Super League side’s longest-serving player, having made 314 appearances since signing in 2014 from Doncaster Belles.

She has won 20 trophies with the reigning league champions and was a key part of their unbeaten campaign last season, captaining Chelsea across 36 games as they won a domestic treble of the league, League Cup and FA Cup.

The centre-back’s decision comes a month after The Athletic reported that she wanted to leave upon her contract’s end at the close of the season, having rejected an extension.

Bright will instead stay on at Chelsea as a trustee of their foundation, and as a club ambassador, the Stamford Bridge side announced on Wednesday.

“Representing Chelsea over the last 12 years has been everything to me, but I’m now ready to say goodbye to playing football,” Bright said in a release on the club’s website.

“I’ve given all I can, and I never wanted to fight for any other badge. It is now time, and I’m ready to go into a new era.

“I’m always going to be Chelsea, but just in a different way.”

Bright announced her international retirement six months ago, calling an end to her England career in October after 88 caps. The centre-back had withdrawn from an England squad that May, saying she was “mentally and physically” at her limits and needed a break.

England head coach Sarina Wiegman paid tribute to the defender after the announcement.

“Millie has played such a big role in the growth of the women’s game, with both England and Chelsea, and she has achieved so much along the way. What she has given to her club and country is incredible,” she said on England’s website.

“It is hard to put into words the impact she has had. She has inspired so many people, pushed standards and shown girls and boys what can be achieved in the sport.”

Bright has won eight WSL titles, six FA Cups, and four Women’s League Cups over her time at Chelsea, encompassing a domestic treble in 2021 to add to last season’s.

With England, she won the 2022 European Championship and received an MBE in 2024 for her services to the game.

Analysis by women’s football writer Charlotte Harpur

The fact the 32-year-old has called time with immediate effect is somewhat surprising but The Athletic reported she was expected to leave the club at the end of the summer following the expiry of her contract. Her future destination, however, was unknown.

Bright has struggled with injuries, an ankle problem has meant she has not featured for Bompastor’s side since February while last summer she underwent minor knee surgery.

The centre-back will go down in history as a Chelsea legend after over a decade at the west London club which has dominated the WSL. Their longest-serving player and record WSL appearance holder has been an integral part of every one of Chelsea’s eight WSL titles and she shared a close bond with former director of women’s football Paul Green who left in February and Chelsea manager Emma Hayes. The USWNT head coach handed the Sheffield-born defender the captain’s armband following Magdalena Eriksson’s departure in 2023.

Bright will be remembered as a combative archetypal no-nonsense defender, strong at tackling and heading the ball and her 5ft 10in frame an asset at defensive and offensive set pieces.

The fact she is staying at the club as a foundation trustee and club ambassador shows her loyalty to a team that she has served since 2015.

“I never wanted to fight for any other badge,” she said.
